method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

items.assessment: All distractors are nonessential theory/brand filler, so recognizing complications is the only reasonable option without interpreting the vignette.
issues: All distractors are nonessential theory/brand filler, so recognizing complications is the only reasonable option without interpreting the vignette.
proposedChanges: Use three credible discharge priorities (supply procurement, routine dressing sequence, moisture protection) competing with escalation signs/contact; state which routine skills have already been demonstrated to make the safety gap decisive.

items.assessment: Drug-name recall and longer pharmacology discussion are irrelevant filler; key is the sole practical response.
issues: Drug-name recall and longer pharmacology discussion are irrelevant filler; key is the sole practical response.
proposedChanges: Use competing practical assessments: availability/cost of supply; adverse effects; caregiving schedule; ability to open packaging. Include confirming cues that other barriers are absent while morning-care conflict persists.

items.assessment: Large print and verbal recall do not plausibly address observed arthritis; longest key uniquely combines every good action.
issues: Large print and verbal recall do not plausibly address observed arthritis; longest key uniquely combines every good action.
proposedChanges: State the client wants independent monitoring and no helper is available during testing. Compare an assessed accessible device/packaging adaptation with caregiver-preopening, repeated use of current packaging and deferral to home nursing. Keep choices similar in length and explain independence/availability cues.

items.assessment: Verbal accuracy versus observed contamination directly distinguishes recall from performance, a meaningful teaching-evaluation contrast; coaching/reassessment key is defensible.
Direct engagement and short interpreted segments support accurate teaching; interpreter decision substitution and unauthorized family involvement are relevant errors.
Bottle colour is filler; key is longest and uniquely includes equipment plus observed practice. Overlaps pharmacology004 oral-syringe selection.
issues: Bottle colour is filler; key is longest and uniquely includes equipment plus observed practice. Overlaps pharmacology004 oral-syringe selection.
proposedChanges: Shift objective to teach-back of actual volume after device already supplied: caregiver draws a concrete incorrect volume, and nurse must identify unit/decimal misunderstanding through a second demonstration. Use plausible measurement interpretations, not colour or theory alone.

items.assessment: Faster repetition and memorizing the discharge summary are cartoon poor teaching; comprehensive key is easily guessed.
issues: Faster repetition and memorizing the discharge summary are cartoon poor teaching; comprehensive key is easily guessed.
proposedChanges: Compare reasonable formats: verbal review in one session; written prioritized action checklist with coached practice; a full technical discharge summary; separate specialist leaflets without a shared sequence. Add a client-specific overload cue and explain why chosen structure fits.

items.assessment: Medical terminology in guide is unrelated filler and permanent family takeover is exaggerated.
issues: Medical terminology in guide is unrelated filler and permanent family takeover is exaggerated.
proposedChanges: Replace option2 with assessment of available family help for guide use; option3 with prior ostomy knowledge. Keep current visual-access assessment key and explain new glasses/avoidance cue; do not use permanent transfer language.

items.assessment: Observed inability despite agreed goal calls for identifying difficult steps and adaptation, rather than equating teaching delivery with learning.
Colour preference replacing intended-use check is obvious nonsense and makes SATA mechanically easy.
issues: Colour preference replacing intended-use check is obvious nonsense and makes SATA mechanically easy.
proposedChanges: Replace option3 with Whether an app-store rating is sufficient evidence of clinical accuracy. Add a fifth option about alignment with intended symptom-tracking purpose as appropriate and vary correct count/positions.

items.assessment: Key is much longer and more specific than vague fitness, neighbour comparison or unrelated weight-only options.
issues: Key is much longer and more specific than vague fitness, neighbour comparison or unrelated weight-only options.
proposedChanges: Use four concrete walking plans of comparable length: mutually agreed short scheduled walks with review (key); prior-activity target despite current baseline; unscheduled walking only when motivation is high; daily distance increases without tolerance checks. Include baseline tolerance and review interval.

items.assessment: Stated benefit and recognized harm create authentic ambivalence; exploring both sides is preferable to imposed quit date or warnings alone.
Restart only after months of smoking is implausible and delays support without rationale.
issues: Restart only after months of smoking is implausible and delays support without rationale.
proposedChanges: Replace option1 with: Reset the same quit plan without discussing the argument. Explain that lapse-trigger review can reveal a missing coping strategy rather than treating calendar restart as sufficient.

items.assessment: Total dietary restriction and small changes cannot affect habits are extreme; only key respects any reasonable care.
issues: Total dietary restriction and small changes cannot affect habits are extreme; only key respects any reasonable care.
proposedChanges: Use plausible alternatives: add several goals at once to maximize benefit; track daily weight instead of the selected behaviour; give general dietary education without specifying when substitution occurs. Explain implementation cue/review rather than merely praise small change.

items.assessment: Triggers and prior attempts are meaningful individualization data; brand alone and nurse-preferred date do not establish readiness or dependence.
Generic comprehensive key is the only safe response against no exercise/faster painful walking; little clinical discrimination.
issues: Generic comprehensive key is the only safe response against no exercise/faster painful walking; little clinical discrimination.
proposedChanges: Add tolerated activity and pain-pattern details. Offer comparable options such as supervised lower-impact trial, shorter painful walks without assessment, stretching-only plan and complete rest until pain-free. Explain why alternative loading preserves goals for stable disease.

items.assessment: Stretching indefinitely and waiting for strength to return spontaneously are implausible extremes.
issues: Stretching indefinitely and waiting for strength to return spontaneously are implausible extremes.
proposedChanges: Replace option1 with return based solely on the old calendar schedule; option3 with flexibility exercises as the only initial plan despite a stated endurance goal. Specify current functional capacity to distinguish gradual progression.

items.assessment: Calories and caffeine do not compete as interventions for prolonged sitting; key can be selected by matching words alone.
issues: Calories and caffeine do not compete as interventions for prolonged sitting; key can be selected by matching words alone.
proposedChanges: Use competing activity plans: planned brief workday movement breaks; longer weekend exercise only; standing continuously without movement variation; tracking step totals without addressing long uninterrupted sitting. Explain sedentary-pattern cue.

items.assessment: Near-duplicate of c-basic066 sodium/serving-size objective; price and advertising are filler.
issues: Near-duplicate of c-basic066 sodium/serving-size objective; price and advertising are filler.
proposedChanges: Replace with an unused applied nutrition objective, e.g. an adult eating plant-based meals who needs to improve non-heme iron absorption: compare adding vitamin-C food with tea/coffee or calcium at that meal. Source-check and write a clinical/dietary context; retain item count with a distinct learning objective.

items.assessment: Budget-sensitive frozen/canned and low-cost protein planning addresses material access without equating nutritional quality with specialty fresh foods.
Heat plus prescribed restriction requires individualized balance; standard unlimited drinking or rigid unchanged limit can each be wrong. This is a useful competing-risk case.
Sleep only on days off is cartoon unsafe; caffeine/screens do not meaningfully compete with the stated household-noise barrier.
issues: Sleep only on days off is cartoon unsafe; caffeine/screens do not meaningfully compete with the stated household-noise barrier.
proposedChanges: Compare environmental/schedule plans: protected dark quiet sleep period (key); longer days-off sleep without household changes; eye mask with sleep time still dictated by family; frequent brief naps in shared living space. Explain protected opportunity rather than generic sleep advice.

items.assessment: Witnessed pauses plus snoring and sleepiness despite adequate opportunity supports breathing-disorder assessment over sleep-hygiene alone.
All distractors concern brand/peer approval/social acceptance, while key bundles every relevant clinical variable and is longest.
issues: All distractors concern brand/peer approval/social acceptance, while key bundles every relevant clinical variable and is longest.
proposedChanges: Use equally relevant assessment questions: usual amount/timing in a typical week (key for quantifying exposure); prior reduction attempts; social pressure; goals for change. Explain why clarifying the undefined exposure precedes tailoring advice.

items.assessment: Clinically feasible combined services and transport support directly address rural access; remote care cannot universally replace examinations.
One treatment for every menopause client is an implausible absolute; broad key dominates by comprehensiveness.
issues: One treatment for every menopause client is an implausible absolute; broad key dominates by comprehensiveness.
proposedChanges: Replace option0 with providing a general hot-flash booklet without asking impact; keep other plausible premature tests/treatment actions and shorten key to Assess symptom burden and individual treatment risks. Add specific history cue if testing options need distinction.

items.assessment: Timely assessment key is sound; dietary iron before follow-up is unrelated to slight new postmenopausal spotting.
issues: Timely assessment key is sound; dietary iron before follow-up is unrelated to slight new postmenopausal spotting.
proposedChanges: Replace option3 with Arrange routine cervical screening as the sole follow-up. Explain new bleeding needs diagnostic assessment of its cause rather than a routine screening substitute.

items.assessment: Key is uniquely long and comprehensive; avoid all activity is an unrealistic opposite.
issues: Key is uniquely long and comprehensive; avoid all activity is an unrealistic opposite.
proposedChanges: Use concise key Arrange bone-risk review and tailor activity/nutrition. Replace total avoidance with flexibility-only activity until bone-density testing; compare plausible but incomplete calcium-only or prior-fitness-based high-impact plans. Add age/history context supporting risk evaluation.

items.assessment: Vigorous stretching and waiting for a fall are implausible; vertebral-fracture key is the only reasonable option.
issues: Vigorous stretching and waiting for a fall are implausible; vertebral-fracture key is the only reasonable option.
proposedChanges: Use competing plans: routine osteoporosis screening at next annual review; treat presumed muscle strain before investigating height loss; increase posture exercises without assessing new pain. Explain height loss plus new back pain warrants earlier fracture/other-cause assessment.

items.assessment: All options are comparable vision observations; functional medication/driver impairment discriminates evaluation need from correction/light preference alone.
Replacing all interaction with writing is an unrealistic restriction; key alone combines two good actions.
issues: Replacing all interaction with writing is an unrealistic restriction; key alone combines two good actions.
proposedChanges: Shorten key to Arrange hearing review and reduce background noise. Replace option3 with provide written group summaries without reviewing hearing/participation barriers; explain why this supports information but does not restore the chosen discussion activity.

items.assessment: Staying home permanently is an exaggerated choice that weakens a clinically useful continence case.
issues: Staying home permanently is an exaggerated choice that weakens a clinically useful continence case.
proposedChanges: Replace option3 with Use absorbent pads for outings without discussing urgency assessment. Explain containment can help but does not establish cause or individualized continence plan.

items.assessment: Only key is comprehensive assessment and longest; generic low-fat advice is implausible for unintentional loss.
issues: Only key is comprehensive assessment and longest; generic low-fat advice is implausible for unintentional loss.
proposedChanges: Recast with concrete assessment data that distinguish physical versus practical causes (e.g. intact swallowing and oral function, partner formerly did shopping/cooking, meals now skipped). Compare equally plausible next assessments/interventions tied to those findings, rather than broad assess-everything key against filler.

items.assessment: Near misses/distance judgment changes require timely functional assessment and interim transport planning rather than age-only decisions or waiting for collision.
Food and complex daily-task ability support individual independence assessment; chronological age/family preference alone do not.
Accepting loneliness as required by retirement is an implausible dismissive distractor.
issues: Accepting loneliness as required by retirement is an implausible dismissive distractor.
proposedChanges: Replace option2 with: Offer an unscheduled list of social services without linking to interests. Explain that a chosen small recurring activity better fits sustained contact and dislike of large groups.

items.assessment: Private goals/prevention assessment addresses later-life sexual health without equating menopause with no infection risk or substituting children for capable adult.
Early values discussion preserves full participation and communicates meaning beyond a form; future emergency-only planning loses that opportunity.
Permanently stopping all caregiving is an exaggerated response to appointment-time cover needs.
issues: Permanently stopping all caregiving is an exaggerated response to appointment-time cover needs.
proposedChanges: Replace option1 with: Reschedule the caregiver appointments repeatedly around the current care routine without arranging replacement help. Explain that recurring supervision gap needs a feasible support plan.

items.assessment: Identical footwear purchase is irrelevant filler as a program outcome.
issues: Identical footwear purchase is irrelevant filler as a program outcome.
proposedChanges: Replace option3 with Staff delivered every planned education session. Explain this measures implementation, while participant attendance/tolerance and sustained goals measure meaningful program uptake.

rubricUpdate: Each item screened for key length/comprehensiveness cues, only-reasonable-answer bias, clinical context, explanation and overlap. Snapshot is immutable; active file may later change.
